title: Edmund and the Static
premise: Jude Underhill investigates impossible accidents in contested orbit, and the strangest one yet involves Edmund Voss, a colony child whose shared dream with forty other children contains details of a massacre that officially never happened—on the very station where Jude's own sister died seven years ago. As corporate archivists scrub records faster than the children can remember them, Jude realizes the 'static' in their cargo manifests is an erasure weapon still running, and that staying invisible has made them complicit. In the end, Jude sacrifices their clean record and freedom to broadcast the children's dream-memory to every settlement in orbit, proving the massacre happened and inheriting, at last, a family worth being seen by.
about_author: Noor Nakamura is a former maritime insurance adjuster turned science fiction writer, drawing on years of reading disaster reports for the human stories buried inside them. They write from a houseboat on the Seto Inland Sea, where they collect oral histories from families of lost sailors.

chapters.title: The Claim That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A routine impossible-accident claim leads Jude to Edmund Voss, a quiet eleven-year-old who describes, in perfect detail, a decompression event on Station Meridian—the same accident file Jude has been unable to close for seven years. The emotional beat is unease: Jude recognizes the child's account as memory, not imagination, because it matches what they saw.

chapters.title: Forty Children, One Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Jude and Edmund. The dream spreads to more children each night, each adding fragments—a name, a corridor number, a scream cut short by static. Corporate liaison Ondine Marsh arrives to 'assist,' and Jude notices records vanishing mid-investigation. The beat is dread hardening into resolve as Jude chooses to protect the children rather than the case.

chapters.title: Static Is a Weapon
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, climax. Tracing the static through old cargo manifests, Jude finds the erasure field's source aboard their own hauler—and learns Marsh intends to wipe the children's memories next, permanently. In a desperate broadcast from the hauler's array, Jude transmits the pooled dream-memory system-wide while Marsh's team storms the deck. The beat is sacrifice: Jude lets themselves be arrested mid-transmission.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, resolution. The broadcast lands; settlements demand answers, the archive lock breaks, and the massacre is entered back into the record under the names the children remembered. Jude, released pending trial, is met at the dock by Edmund and the other kids—who have claimed Jude as theirs. The beat is belonging: inheritance isn't what you're left, it's who stays.
